narrativeProgression.description: Fungai's personal definition of art and her vision for creating an accessible art studio in Zimbabwe.

Fungai defines art as a process of open-minded exploration, seeking answers, and giving voice to the voiceless. She highlights her desire to share her knowledge and opportunities with those who lack access.

Fungai elaborates on her dream of establishing a printmaking studio in Zimbabwe, emphasizing the importance of providing creative spaces for individuals from diverse backgrounds to express themselves.

Fungai addresses the question of affordability in art, acknowledging the financial challenges while emphasizing the importance of pursuing one's passion and finding ways to make it work. She concludes by expressing gratitude for the support she has received.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I believe that practicing art opens up your mind.
What is going to look like? I'm not entirely sure.
Because with most of the work that I've done in the past, I sort of... I don't know if this is the right word, but I sort of go with the flow.
So with some of the images I sketch them out, I don't necessarily want to trace out or get the exact image of a photograph that I find.
So therefore using freehand is something that I've decided to sort of... I've always used freehand in my work.
But mostly in prints I find that sometimes when it's almost perfect, that's where people appreciate it a lot more.
But then I do feel that because it's about me and it's quite personal, it has to be something that's quite freehand and quite emotional.
So what you will expect to see in my work is sort of maybe a lot more expressive work.
And there will be quite small prints because there's something that's quite close to me and I don't really want it to blow up into a massive print or a massive painting or anything.
So they're quite small prints and I suppose maybe just thinking into the future, maybe how I would show them or be in chronological order.
So...
They are prints but how I start them off is sort of like freehand because I use my technique as a dry point and I draw onto copper with a dry point needle.
So that's freehand really sort of like a pencil on paper.
So yeah, I learned to add to my uni actually.
I'd always sort of scratched into plastic which was because it's a lot more affordable.
So that's what I use but then I then found that doing it on copper gives it a really nice feel to my prints.
But I learned that at a university and it's something that is quite personal and quite intimate because it's sort of like an experience when I'm actually scratching into the plate.
So that's why I've found it quite fulfilling.
Okay, so I believe that practicing art opens up your mind.
You're constantly in search of answers and you want to know more and you want to say, you want to help that person that doesn't have the ability to say anything.
You want to give other people that don't have voices, voices.

And how I would tell myself successful when I can sort of give back what I've been given, give back the opportunity to express myself to other people that are not necessarily in positions that they can do so.
So something that is quite passionate, that I'm quite passionate about is definitely having a studio of my own in Zimbabwe for printmaking.
Not that there aren't any things that are really happening, there of course there are not more creative things that are happening in Zimbabwe.
But I do feel that you could never have enough of institutions that are willing to expand creativity, have children from all different backgrounds, come in one place and just open up their minds.

And think about the things that people don't would not necessarily just come up to them and just tell them, figure out themselves, figure out who they are through art because this is what I've been, it's a privilege that I've been put in a position like this.
Well, I would have loved to say I had a loan but I actually didn't have a loan I had to work for money. I had to work really and it's a passion of mine.
I do believe in anything, anything can be quite costly. If you get into any field you have to buy books to study, you have to buy stationary.
And that's like me when you buy a book instead of me buying a book to read, sit down and read and study, I will buy materials.
It is pricey and I do see why people would be quite discouraged. But when you know that it's a passion of yours, you will find a way.
You will find a way, you will work constantly so that you can just buy one plate of copper.

In anything that you truly enjoy, anything that you truly love and not that I'm saying that those people that decided not to do truly did not love it, it depends on the circumstances they are on as well.
And I believe I've been fortunate rather apart from being passionate, I have been fortunate to have people that actually do support me.
